messages:
sam: Install help — fresh M2 mac, followed quickstart and ran `brew install redwoodctl`. Installer finished but `redwoodctl` not found. also `redwoodctl login` opens browser but CLI never receives the callback. stuck on \"waiting for auth callback\".
anya: check /opt/homebrew/bin is in PATH and whether the formula auto-linked. `brew list redwoodctl` and `brew link --overwrite redwoodctl` can fix missing bin.
sam: `brew list redwoodctl` shows files under /opt/homebrew/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.6/bin but /opt/homebrew/bin wasn't on my PATH because of an old zshrc. linked and restarted shell, binary works now. login still stalls.
kevin: corporate browser / extension sometimes blocks the loopback callback. Try `redwoodctl login --no-browser` to get a code you can paste into another device. also try `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost redwoodctl login` if you have proxy envs set.
sam: `env | grep -i proxy` shows HTTPS_PROXY set. unsetting that and re-running fixed the browser callback. CLI logged in and wrote profile \"work\" to ~/.redwood/config.
anya: nice. quick note: if you used sudo at any point the config dir might be root-owned. do `ls -la ~/.redwood` and `sudo chown -R $(whoami) ~/.redwood` if needed.
sam: aha mine was root-owned because i tried a different installer earlier. chowned and all good. now running `redwoodctl dev start` fails with \"could not bind to 127.0.0.1:8910\". i thought dev uses 8910 by default?
kevin: yes default is 8910. EADDRINUSE means something else is listening. `lsof -i TCP:8910` or `lsof -i :3000` can reveal conflicts. Docker port forwarding sometimes grabs 3000 even with no containers.
sam: lsof showed node PID 7864 listening on 3000 from a leftover local process. killed it and dev start booted. also discovered the CLI wrote duplicate profile entries because i aborted login midway; YAML kept the first key so SDK picked the wrong one.
anya: `redwoodctl profile list` will show active profiles and expiry on newer CLIs. If you don't have that, upgrade brew package. Also add validation to the config read path so duplicates warn. filing INF-4901.
ci-bot: note: INF-4901 (cli: warn on duplicate profile keys), INF-4902 (cli: detect proxy env and suggest NO_PROXY), INF-4903 (dev: better EADDRINUSE hint) created and linked to backlog.
devex-bot: docs: https://redwood.company/docs/devex/cli-troubleshoot covers PATH, headless login, proxy guidance, and profile management.
sam: final summary for anyone else: 1) ensure Homebrew bin is on PATH and don't mix sudo, 2) unset HTTPS_PROXY or set NO_PROXY for localhost, 3) use `--no-browser` as fallback, 4) `lsof` to find port conflicts, 5) use `redwoodctl profile list` to verify which profile SDKs will pick. thanks! :thumbsup:
